# Microsoft MakeCode

> > Microsoft MakeCode is a block-based and text-based programming platform for creating interactive coding experiences across micro:bit, Minecraft Education, Arcade games, and physical computing devices.

MakeCode supports educators and learners with visual programming (Blocks), JavaScript, and Python across multiple editors including MakeCode Arcade for retro game development, Minecraft Education for in-game coding, and micro:bit for physical computing. The platform includes comprehensive curricula, tutorials, and tools for both beginners and advanced developers.

## Key Topics

- MakeCode Arcade
- micro:bit
- Minecraft Education
- Block-based programming
- JavaScript
- Python
- Game development
- Visual programming
- CS education curricula
- Tutorials and skillmaps
- PXT framework
- Adafruit Circuit Playground Express
- LEGO MINDSTORMS Education EV3
- GitHub integration
- Extensions and customization

## Getting Started

- [Microsoft MakeCode](https://makecode.com): Main homepage for Microsoft MakeCode learn-to-code platform
- [About](https://makecode.com/about): About Microsoft MakeCode framework for interactive programming experiences
- [About MakeCode Arcade](https://arcade.makecode.com/about): About MakeCode Arcade retro game editor for browser and handheld consoles
- [Intro to MakeCode Arcade](https://arcade.makecode.com/tutorials/intro): Beginner tutorial for MakeCode Arcade basics and workspace navigation
- [Introducing Microsoft MakeCode](https://makecode.com/blog/makecode-overview): Launch blog post introducing Microsoft MakeCode platform and micro:bit

## Tutorials and Learning Paths

- [Tutorials](https://arcade.makecode.com/tutorials): Collection of MakeCode Arcade game development tutorials and activities
- [Skillmaps](https://arcade.makecode.com/skillmaps): Guided tutorial sequences for learning Arcade game development skills
- [Agent Build](https://minecraft.makecode.com/tutorials/agent-build): Minecraft tutorial teaching agent block placement and movement commands

## Computer Science Curricula

- [Introduction to Computer Science with Microsoft MakeCode Arcade](https://arcade.makecode.com/courses/introCS): Full-year high school CS curriculum using MakeCode Arcade and game-based learning
- [About this Course](https://minecraft.makecode.com/courses/csintro/about): Middle school CS intro course overview using MakeCode and Minecraft
- [About CS Intro 2](https://arcade.makecode.com/courses/csintro2/about): About CS Intro 2 course: programming language, teachers, and authors
- [About CS Intro 4](https://arcade.makecode.com/courses/csintro4/about): About CS Intro 4 course: programming language, style, and teacher resources

## Documentation and Reference

- [Documentation](https://arcade.makecode.com/docs): Main documentation hub for MakeCode Arcade game development resources
- [MakeCode (PXT) Documentation](https://makecode.com/docs): Technical documentation for PXT framework and creating MakeCode editors
- [Developer Tips and Tricks](https://arcade.makecode.com/developer): Advanced developer guide for customizing and extending MakeCode Arcade
- [MakeCode Tools](https://makecode.com/tools): Collection of MakeCode developer tools: GitHub Explorer, Playground, etc.

## Creating Content

- [Tutorials](https://makecode.com/writing-docs/tutorials): Guide for authoring step-by-step tutorials in markdown format
- [Tutorial basics](https://makecode.com/writing-docs/tutorials/basics): Tutorial markdown structure and formatting basics for MakeCode

## Community and Support

- [Microsoft MakeCode Blog](https://makecode.com/blog): MakeCode blog with updates, interviews, and CS education announcements
- [Help and Questions](https://forum.makecode.com/t/help-and-questions/1335): Community forum for asking questions and debugging Arcade code
- [FAQ](https://forum.makecode.com/faq): Forum FAQ with code of conduct and community guidelines

## Optional

- [Community](https://arcade.makecode.com/community): Showcase of games submitted by the MakeCode Arcade community
- [Help translate](https://arcade.makecode.com/translate): Guide for volunteering to translate MakeCode Arcade via Crowdin
